blocks.text: Imagine building a skyscraper without blueprints. Software architecture documentation serves as these blueprints, guiding development and evolution.

blocks.markdown: In software engineering, documenting architecture is crucial for maintaining clarity and consistency as a system evolves. This unit explores how to effectively document architectural decisions, manage technical debt, and evolve architecture without resorting to a complete rewrite.

blocks.title: Architectural Decision Record (ADR)
blocks.text: An Architectural Decision Record is a document that captures an important architectural decision made along with its context and consequences.

blocks.markdown: Architectural Decision Records (ADRs) are vital for tracking the rationale behind key decisions in a software project. They help future developers understand why certain paths were chosen and the trade-offs involved.

blocks.title: Creating an ADR
blocks.prompt: Document an architectural decision to use a microservices architecture over a monolithic one.

steps.text: Identify the decision to be documented.
Describe the context of the decision.
steps.latex: Context: The system needs to scale independently and handle diverse workloads.

steps.text: List the consequences of the decision.
steps.latex: Consequences: Increased complexity in deployment, but improved scalability and fault isolation.

blocks.answer: An ADR for choosing microservices would include the decision, context, and consequences as outlined.

blocks.title: Technical Debt
blocks.text: Technical debt refers to the implied cost of additional rework caused by choosing an easy solution now instead of using a better approach that would take longer.

blocks.markdown: Technical debt is a metaphor reflecting the future cost of maintaining and evolving a system due to shortcuts taken during development. While sometimes necessary, it must be managed carefully to avoid crippling future progress.

blocks.title: Evaluating Technical Debt
blocks.prompt: A team decides to skip writing unit tests to meet a deadline. Evaluate this decision in terms of technical debt.

steps.latex: Cost: Increased risk of defects and higher maintenance costs.

blocks.answer: The decision incurs technical debt by increasing future maintenance costs and defect risks.

blocks.markdown: Evolving software architecture involves making incremental changes to improve the system without a complete rewrite. This requires careful planning and documentation to ensure that changes align with the overall architectural goals.

blocks.title: Evolving Architecture
blocks.text: Evolving architecture involves refactoring, modularization, and sometimes re-architecting parts of the system to meet new requirements or improve performance.

points: Architectural Decision Records (ADRs) document important decisions, their context, and consequences.
Technical debt is the cost of shortcuts taken during development, which can hinder future progress.
Evolving architecture without a rewrite involves careful planning and incremental changes.
